jupyter: py-viz

```{python}
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Set the theme (Similar to theme_minimal() in ggplot)
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# 2. Load tidy data
tips = sns.load_dataset("tips")

# 3. Plotting (The ggplot2 equivalent)
# x/y = aes(x, y), hue = aes(color), col = facet_wrap
sns.relplot(
    data=tips, 
    x="total_bill", y="tip", 
    hue="day", col="time",
    kind="scatter"
) # Semicolon is crucial to stop extra text output in Molten!
```


```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from IPython.display import display

# Create a sample DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Variable": ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta"],
    "Value": np.random.randn(4),
    "Category": ["A", "B", "A", "B"]
})

# 1. Standard Jupyter-style display
# This uAually renders with better spacing/bold headers
display(df)

# 2. Add some "Styling" (The 'Tidy' way to highlight data)
# This will show you if Molten/Terminal can handle color-coding
styled_df = df.style.background_gradient(cmap='viridis')


display(styled_df)```
